findings.explanation: env_reset is always on in sudo-rs, so this line has no effect.
findings.fix: No change needed. You can remove the option.

findings.explanation: sudo-rs never sends mail, so mail_badpass has no effect. It is accepted for compatibility.
findings.fix: No change needed. You can remove the option.

findings.explanation: sudo-rs 0.2.13 does not know the Defaults option "requiretty" ("unknown setting"). sudo-rs does not implement requiretty on purpose (sudo-rs FAQ, "Why did you change X?"). sudo-rs reports a syntax error and skips the whole line, so nothing else on it takes effect either.
findings.fix: Remove requiretty from this line, or move it to its own Defaults line so the other options still apply.

findings.explanation: Wildcard in argument /etc/logrotate.d/*. sudo-rs only allows a wildcard in arguments as a final, standalone * ("wildcards are not allowed in command arguments"). sudo-rs reports a syntax error and skips the whole line, so nothing else on it takes effect either.
findings.fix: List the exact arguments allowed, or put a single * as the last argument to allow any arguments. Wildcards in the command path itself are still fine.

findings.explanation: The LOG_OUTPUT tag is ignored by sudo-rs. The rule still applies, but sudo-rs has no I/O logging or mail, and visudo -c from sudo-rs reports the tag ("this tag is ignored by sudo-rs").
findings.fix: Remove LOG_OUTPUT:. Use auditd or session recording outside sudo if you need I/O logs.

findings.explanation: Wildcard in host name db*.internal. The sudo-rs parser only accepts letters, digits, '.', '-' and '_' in host names ("expected host name"), even though its manual still describes host wildcards. sudo-rs reports a syntax error and skips the whole line, so nothing else on it takes effect either.
findings.fix: List each host name, or use a Host_Alias, or ALL.

findings.explanation: This rule lets a user edit specific files with sudoedit. USN-8708-1 (1 September 2026) fixed a race in sudo-rs sudoedit that let such a user place files in any directory and possibly gain root. It only affects systems with fine-grained sudoedit rules like this one. On Ubuntu 26.04 the fix is in sudo-rs 0.2.13-0ubuntu1.2.
findings.fix: Run apt update && apt upgrade, and check with: dpkg-query -W sudo-rs
